root_cause: When a focused element inside the focus trap is removed from the DOM, the browser moves focus to the document body. The focusin handler (checkFocusIn) detects focus on the body but the trap's mostRecentlyFocusedNode still references the detached element. The recovery logic in the else branch attempts to focus the detached node, which fails, leaving focus on the body.
repair_strategy: Add an early guard in checkFocusIn to clear the mostRecentlyFocusedNode if it is no longer attached to the document (using the existing isNodeAttached utility). This ensures the recovery logic falls back to the initial focus node.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped inside the dialog after removing an item, preserving tab order and preventing focus loss to background elements.
functional_risks: The isNodeAttached check may have performance implications if called frequently, but it's only on focusin events. It correctly handles shadow DOM and detached nodes.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on the remove button of an item, the count updates and focus stays inside the basket (#basket:focus-within is true).
Tab navigation continues to wrap correctly within the dialog after item removal.
